history.summary: Rohtak has more than one Sheetla Mata shrine, so the CSV's generic name is ambiguous (identity flag): the best match is the Prachin Shri Sheetla Mata Mandir at Tej Colony, Rohtak (4.4 stars, ~2 km from Rohtak Junction), though there is also a Sheetla Mata Mandir on Jind Road, Singhpura Khurd. Devotees come for the goddess of disease and healing (Sheetla is invoked against smallpox and fevers), and for the mundan (first haircut) ceremony of infants, which local tradition holds is done at the goddess's feet. The 18th-century legends associating Sheetla with Kripi / Guru Dronacharya's wife belong to the Gurugram Masani shrine, NOT this Rohtak temple - do not conflate the two. Founding date and history of the Rohtak temple are UNVERIFIED.

name: Sheetla Mata Temple
town_description: Rohtak is a major city in Haryana, about 70 km from Delhi, and an important education and commercial hub of the state, home to Maharshi Dayanand University. The city has ancient roots, with nearby archaeological sites at Khokhra Kot linked to the Indus Valley and later periods. It is well connected by rail and road on the Delhi-Hisar corridor.
